result.title: Structured Extraction of Diffraction Data from Covalent Organic Frameworks
result.comment: 66 pages: main text (19 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables) and Supporting Information (47 pages) in one file. Data and code: https://github.com/AaronG211/pxrd_PEAK ; database website: https://pxrd-peak.vercel.app
result.summary: Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) is the primary structural evidence for covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and many other materials. Yet decades of measured patterns exist only as images in published figures. Automatic recovery is difficult, because PXRD figures vary widely in format, from a single curve to crowded stacks with labels, insets, and neighboring plots that challenge traditional computer vision. This work presents a pipeline in which a vision large language model (LLM) interprets the layout of each figure, locating the diffraction plot and its curves and sketching a coarse trace of each, while classical computer vision (CV) refines every trace to pixel-level accuracy. Applied to 3,954 COF articles, the pipeline produces 11,445 calibrated diffraction curves, released in the open database COF-PEAK. Compared with a hand digitization of 60 panels, extracted peak positions differ by a median of only 0.07 degrees. Whereas papers usually report only a few peak angles, which limits further analysis, the digitized curves enable tracking how peak prominence, a possible marker of crystallinity, changes with synthesis conditions. Vision LLMs and classical CV can thus turn such figures into reusable experimental data.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作构建了一条从 COF 文献的 PXRD 图像中自动提取衍射曲线的流程：由视觉大模型解析图幅布局并给出粗略描迹，再用经典 CV 精修到像素级，最终发布 COF-PEAK 数据库。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于科学图表数据数字化与数据库构建，视觉模型仅用于版面和曲线定位，不涉及推理状态、证据筛选或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的具体联系。
